chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said:

Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) instructed me regarding some needs of his in al-Madinah, so I went out. While I was between the pass of al-Rawha’ upon my mount, suddenly there was a man waving his garment. He said: I turned toward him and thought that he was thirsty, so I handed him the water-skin, but he said to me, ‘I have no need of it,’ and he handed me a letter, the clay seal of which was still moist.

He said: When I looked at the seal, it was the seal of Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام). So I said, ‘When was your meeting with the owner of the letter?’ He said, ‘Just now.’ And in the letter were matters commanding me to do them. Then I turned around, and there was no one with me.

He said: Then Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) arrived, and I met him and said, ‘May I be made your ransom, a man came to me with your letter while its clay seal was still moist.’ So he said, ‘O Sadir, we have servants from among the jinn, and when we desire speed, we send them.’ And in another narration, he said: ‘We have followers from among the jinn just as we have followers from among humankind, so when we intend a matter, we send them.’

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (عليه السلام), the Imam mentioned in the narration
key_terms.أَتْبَاعًا: followers or adherents who obey and assist
key_terms.السُّرْعَةَ: quickness or speed in carrying out a matter
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, unseen beings who are described here as servants or followers
key_terms.الْخَاتَمِ: the seal identifying the letter as belonging to the Imam
key_terms.خَدَمًا: servants employed to carry out a task swiftly
key_terms.كِتَابًا: a written letter or message sent by the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kafi describe the jinn serving or following the Imams (عليهم السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) sent a message through an unseen messenger, later explained as being from the jinn who serve or follow the Imams (عليهم السلام). The report highlights the extraordinary means by which the Imam’s commands could be carried and points to the recognition of the Imam’s authority among both humans and jinn.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balad, from Sadeyr Al Sayrafi who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> ordered me to deal with a need of his<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Medina, so I went out. So while I was between Fajj Al-Raeha upon my ride, when a person waved his cloth at me. So I inclined towards him and thought that he is thirsty. So I gave him the drinking cup, but he said to me, ‘There is no need for me with it’, and he gave me a letters, the ink of which was still wet.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So when I looked at the seal, it was the seal of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’. So I said, ‘When did he<sup>asws</sup>, the owner of the letter pact with you?’  He said, ‘Just now’. And there were things in the letter instructing me with these. Then I turned around, but there was no one in my presence.

Then I proceeded to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and met up with him<sup>asws</sup>, and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man came over to me with your<sup>asws</sup> letter and its ink was still wet’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Sadeyr! For us there are servants from the Jinn. So whenever we<sup>asws</sup> intend the quickness, we<sup>asws</sup> send them’. And in another report, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For us<sup>asws</sup> there are followers from the Jinn just as there are followers from the human beings. So, whenever we<sup>asws</sup> intend a matter, we<sup>asws</sup> send them’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from Sadir al-Sayrafi who has said the following.

“Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) asked me to help him in a few things in Maina. I left and when reached fajj al-Rawha’ a man waved to me with his cloths. The narrator has said that I turned to him and I though he was thirsty. I offered the cup but he declined saying, “I do not need it.” He gave a letter with its ink still not dried up.

The narrator has said that when looked at it, it had the seal of abu Ja‘far (a.s.) on. I asked him when were you in the presence of abu Ja‘far (a.s.)?” He said, “Just now I was in his presence.” In the letter there were few things that he had commanded me to do. When looked around there was no one with me.”

The narrator has said that then I went to meet abu Ja‘far (a.s.) and said, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, a man came to me with your letter the ink of which was not yet dried up.” He said, “O Sadir, we servants from Jinns. When we would need a thing to happen quickly we send them to do it.”
